note:
The household of Alfred Charles Radford, lace manufacturer (sewers and embroidery), at Gladstone House, Lincoln Circus (#201). Sent as 1921, but the ages fix it as the 1911 return: Alfred is 45 and Doris Mary 13 here, while the record's 1921 entries have them at 56 and 23. Alfred (#1195), Nellie (#1196) and Doris Mary (#1197) were in the record only for 1921, unfiled under 'Lincoln Circus 1', and are bound by number so they gain 1911; Leslie Stafford and the two servants are new.

Wright's Directory of Nottingham prints 'Gladstone house, Radford Alfd. Chas' on Lincoln Circus in 1910-11, 1913-14 and 1915-16. The record also files an 1911 household at Gladstone House: Edward Palmer, gardener, his family, and a cook, parlourmaid and housemaid. With the directory giving the house to the Radfords, and the Radfords' own servants being Nutt and Morley, that filing wants checking against its return; it is not moved here. Frances Lillian Nutt's birthplace is transcribed 'Jean, Staffordshire', which is not a place, and is kept as Staffordshire. Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way.
source: 1911 census, Gladstone House, Lincoln Circus, transcribed by A. Hagues. Directory evidence: Wright's Directory of Nottingham 1910-11, page 124 (Leicester Special Collections id 165800); 1913-14, page 141 (Leicester Special Collections id 166497); 1915-16, page 143 (Leicester Special Collections id 347784).
